**My thinking as this farmer:**

I've been working this land for 25 years. My wheat and maize give me stable food and income — I follow the same rotation my neighbors do because it works here in Quzhou. My son helps sometimes but he works in the city now, so I have to be careful about how much labor I take on. Cotton pays more per mu when the price is good, but it's hard work at harvest time.

I'll split the land like I always do: 16 mu for wheat going into maize, and 8 mu for cotton on the other plots.

For **wheat**, I'll plant the improved seed I buy from the village cooperative — better than the old seed I kept myself. I'll irrigate three times like usual: once before planting, once at jointing, once at filling. My neighbor skipped the jointing irrigation last year and his yield dropped. Not doing that. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and urea at jointing. Two pesticide sprays — one for weeds in winter, one for rust and aphids in spring.

For **maize**, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no-till to save time and moisture. Hybrid seed is just what you use now, everyone does. Summer rains help but I'll pump the well twice — once at planting if it's dry, once before silking since that's when it matters most.

For **cotton**, I'll plough in spring and transplant seedlings in April. Cotton needs more water and more spraying, but 8 mu is manageable for me alone. I use Bt hybrid seed so I don't have to spray for bollworm as much as the old days. Still need to watch for spider mites and whitefly. Four irrigations — cotton is thirsty and our summers get dry.
